set.approach: From Jasper, drive toward Hinton and turn onto the road to Miette Hot Springs. A viewpoint on that road shows the ridge and is a good place to study the routes. Beyond the hairpin turn, leave the car in a small left-hand pullout and take the faint path that drops to the river. Cross the river at the right spot, which is usually about knee deep outside spring and wet weather. On the far side, go left to the break in the first big cliff band, then trend right and scramble through two smaller bands, using faint forest trails where you can find them; much of this is bushwhacking.

review.notes: Ashlar Ridge page.

set.approach: From Jasper, take the Icefields Parkway south to Athabasca Falls, take the old highway (93A) there, and continue past the falls to Leech Lake. Park in the pullout there, or in the small one a little farther on the left. A well-kept trail leads into the forest and reaches the crag in a short walk.

review.notes: Lost Boys area page: access via 93A, pullout and trail; same crag access for all its sectors.

set.approach: Start from the Castle Mountain fire lookout and head north, uphill, on a trail that gets steeper to a gully, cross the drainage heading east and pick the trail up again. It continues steeply to the bottom of the hut access trail, where rappel bolts show above. From there go left, to the west, a short way to a bowl-shaped wall; the first-pitch bolts are easy to see.
set.descent_text: The simplest way off is to walk: from the top, head east across the plateau toward the Castle Mountain hut, then descend the hut access trail, which has a few short fourth-class downclimbs and an optional rappel, back to the base of the wall and the lookout. Belay anchors on the route are fixed for rappelling.

review.notes: Bastion route page: approach from the lookout and the walk-off.

set.approach: Take the Rockbound Lake trail to the turnoff for the Lost Lemon crag, continue a short way farther, then head up and left through forest to a drainage. The prow of the route is obvious once you reach the wall.
set.descent_text: From the upper anchor, traverse the ledge to the right: a steep hike above the lower cliff band, with bolts for the first stretch if you want to stay roped. The second half is lower-angled; stay high until you can curve around the corner onto the east side and pick up the trail back down.

review.notes: Gripped article on The Moat: approach and descent.

set.approach: The trailhead is a roadside pullout on Highway 16 east of Jasper, on the right when heading toward Jasper from Hinton, just past a bridge, and a garbage bin marks it. Walk from the back of the pullout onto the established hiking trail to Cinquefoil Mountain, and stay on it until the crag shows ahead. Where the path splits faintly short of a rounded rise, bear right, then follow the switchbacks and cross a meadow to the foot of the cliff.

review.notes: One area page for the pullout, trail, fork, switchbacks and meadow.

set.approach: Park in the large pullout with an outhouse on Highway 16 near Hidden Valley, on the right when driving from Jasper and on the left from Hinton. Start the trail at the end of the pullout opposite the outhouse, go around a pond, climb a steep hill of coal and shale, and then follow the obvious trail up and to the left to the cliffs.

review.notes: Hidden Valley area page: pullout, trail, pond, hill, cliffs.

set.approach: Park in the small roadside pullout just before the bridge on Highway 16, where wooden signs point toward Roche Ronde and Smet. Across the road, climb the obvious trail up the left side of a blasted cliff face, and at the first fork take the faint left branch, which is easy to miss; you are on the right trail when you walk along a grassy ridge with gentle drops on both sides. Follow it up to a marked ridge, which is the top of the wall, then continue to a pair of small spruce trees beside a cairn, where the climbers' trail starts. It passes a downward scramble protected by wire cable and reaches the base of the wall, with the obvious face on your left and low first bolts.

review.notes: Juno Wall page: parking, trail, fork, cairn, cable scramble, base.

set.approach: From the first Medicine Lake viewpoint on Maligne Lake Road, follow the far shore of the lake, away from the road, as far as Watchtower Creek, then follow the creek upstream, picking up a trail. The trail ends at a bridge made of planks; cross it and you are at the wall. Spring runoff can make the creek crossing and the shoreline impassable.

review.notes: Watchtower Creek area page plus the Kiss the Sky Wall page for the plank bridge; high water caution from the area page.

set.approach: Park in the round, sandy pullout on the Icefields Parkway south of the Kerkeslin campground entrance. Behind it, pass through a gap in the trees into a small hidden field and head toward Kerkeslin crag, taking the narrow trail that bears slightly right through poplar forest, where it steepens. Shortly after leaving the aspens, take the fork to the left; if you can already see short cliffs ahead before turning, you have gone too far, so go back a short way to the fork. The new trail then follows a creek up a narrow canyon to the walls.

review.notes: Youth Lagoon area page.

set.approach: Park in the paved roadside pullout on Highway 16 (on the right from Jasper, on the left from Hinton), before the big bushes. Walk west beside the highway a short way until an obvious trail leaves on the left and follow it across marshy ground to the foot of the wall. The wall is visible from the road, and other routes lie farther left along its base.

review.notes: Merlin Wall page: pullout, short road walk, marsh trail.

set.approach: Park at the pullout on the west side of the Icefields Parkway by Hector Creek and pick up the Mount Hector trail on the south side of the drainage. It runs through forest, along the left edge of an avalanche bowl and on to the lip of a waterfall. Cross the creek there into the small hanging valley between Andromache and Little Hector, then follow cairns and goat trails up a series of benches and an easy gully to the upper benches. Cross left over a bowl with a big boulder, follow the dry watercourse to the base of the towers and continue to the farthest-left bowl. The right-hand tower is easily mistaken for the spire. The route starts below and left of a big black roof, at a one-bolt station on a small ledge.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route on fixed anchors, using a 60 m rope; the first rappel is from the summit ring-bolts. Two of the stations are reached by short walks or scrambles along ledges, and one long rappel is overhanging with a stiff pull, so knot the rope ends. At the foot of the route, follow the cairns back down the approach to the highway.

review.notes: Achilles Spire route page.

set.approach: Drive Maligne Lake Road to the pullout near the two boulders on the left, beyond the picnic area on the right. From there a trail climbs past a boulder field to the slab.

review.notes: Rainy Day Slab page; distances omitted as single-sourced.

set.approach: From Jasper, take the Icefields Parkway south to Athabasca Falls, take the old highway (93A) there, and continue past the falls to Leech Lake. Park in the pullout there, or in the small one a little farther on the left. A well-kept trail leads into the forest and reaches the crag in a short walk.

review.notes: Lost Boys area page: access via 93A, pullout and trail; same crag access for all its sectors.

set.approach: Take Maligne Lake Road from Highway 16 east of Jasper and park at the bridge pullout on the left. Cross the bridge, turn left into the forest in the direction of the next bridge, and shortly turn right onto the marked trail that climbs a steep hill. Where the marked trail veers right, keep left on an unmarked trail and follow it through open Douglas fir forest until a drop-off appears on your left. Turn right and go downhill to reach Rock Gardens; going downhill and left leads to Boulder Gardens instead.

review.notes: Rock Gardens area page.

set.approach: Park in the large pullout on Highway 16 near the Hidden Valley lot, with an outhouse nearby, and start along the trail at the east end of the Hidden Valley parking area. A small pond may need crossing on logs. The trail braids into goat paths and then turns up the valley; follow the orange flagging, small rock cages and cairns toward the base of the cliff. The first few routes begin on the first buttress; continue along the cliff line past an obvious wide break to the second buttress, which holds most of the routes.

review.notes: Syncline area page: trail, markers, buttress order.

set.approach: Park in the small pullout on Highway 16 with a distinctive gate at the back. Follow the creek bed, watching for a thin path along the left bank; it is easier and safer to walk on the bank than to pick through the boulders in the creek. Pass tall sand towers on your right and enter a small canyon, where water-polished limestone can be slippery. The cliff comes into view shortly after the canyon opens out.

review.notes: Shredder Reef area page.

set.approach: Park in the large pullout with an outhouse on Highway 16 near Hidden Valley, on the right when driving from Jasper and on the left from Hinton. Start the trail at the end of the pullout opposite the outhouse, go around a pond, climb a steep hill of coal and shale, and then follow the obvious trail up and to the left to the cliffs.

review.notes: Hidden Valley area page: pullout, trail, pond, hill, cliffs.

set.approach: From the first Medicine Lake viewpoint on Maligne Lake Road, follow the far shore of the lake, away from the road, as far as Watchtower Creek, then follow the creek upstream, picking up a trail. The wall sits in the same creek drainage as Kiss the Sky Wall. Spring runoff can make the creek crossing and the shoreline impassable.

review.notes: Watchtower Creek area page: shared approach for its sectors.

set.approach: Park in the round, sandy pullout on the Icefields Parkway south of the Kerkeslin campground entrance. Behind it, pass through a gap in the trees into a small hidden field and head toward Kerkeslin crag, taking the narrow trail that bears slightly right through poplar forest, where it steepens. Shortly after leaving the aspens, take the fork to the left; if you can already see short cliffs ahead before turning, you have gone too far, so go back a short way to the fork. The new trail then follows a creek up a narrow canyon to the walls.

review.notes: Youth Lagoon area page.
